findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction for TL0 users
findings.body: `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so for a trust-level-0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor the serializer omits it (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always emitted and exposes the host (and, for same-domain URLs, the full path) of the very field that was deliberately hidden. This defeats the anti-spam/privacy protection: a TL0 spammer's domain is still visible to anonymous users through `website_name`. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (or its `include_...?` should delegate to the same check).

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark so it is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks up conditional inclusion methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is dead code and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting `"website_name": null` for every user without a website and adding noise to every user payload. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: String mutation with `<<` on a literal in the suffix check
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` mutates the receiver string literal in place instead of concatenating with `+`. It happens to work today because the literal is recreated on each call, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment this file gets `# frozen_string_literal: true` (which Discourse added file-by-file), and it is needlessly destructive. Use `"." + website_host` or string interpolation.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case URLs are treated as a different domain
findings.body: `URI#host` preserves the case the user typed, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is lower-case. For a profile website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an `example.com` instance, `website_host == discourse_host` is false and all the subsequent suffix comparisons fail too, so the full path is not shown and the feature silently does nothing. Downcase `website_host` (and the host used for the suffix/segment comparisons) before comparing.

findings.title: Repeated URI parsing and only one of the branches handles sub/parent domains
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times per call (once for the host, again in each branch for the path) even though a single parsed object would do; the `rescue nil` only guards the first parse, so an input that parses inconsistently would raise from the later unguarded `URI(...)` calls. Additionally the sibling-domain branch only strips a single label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so a website like `blog.example.com` on an `example.com` instance is not recognised as the same domain. Parse once into a local variable and compare registrable domains consistently.

findings.title: TL0/anonymous spec does not assert that website_name is withheld
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in this spec (used by the "doesn't serialize untrusted attributes" example) still contains only the old fields, so the new `website_name` attribute is not covered. As a result the spec passes even though `website_name` is serialized for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous visitor, leaking the restricted website value. Add `website_name` to the list once the serializer is fixed.

findings.title: The sibling-subdomain branch of website_name is untested
findings.body: The three new examples cover only the exact-match case and the "website host is a suffix of the instance host" case (both of which go through the first `if` and the final `else`). The most intricate branch, the equal-label-count comparison at user_serializer.rb:144-146 (e.g. website `www.example.com` on instance `forum.example.com`, and the negative case `www.example.com` vs `forum.other.com`), has no coverage, as does the blank/invalid-website path that returns nil. These are the branches most likely to regress.
